key_insight: Gaussian spatial weighting in PINNs can automatically focus training on sharp Burgers shocks, improving discontinuity capture without knowing shock location in advance.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more practical for flow problems with moving fronts or shocks, where accurate localization is critical for reliable CFD surrogate modeling and inverse analysis.
method: Add a Gaussian-based spatial weight to the physics loss.
Let the residual landscape drive adaptive emphasis on high-gradient regions.
Train without prior shock-location information to track stationary and moving discontinuities.
evidence_signal: On 1D low-viscosity Burgers cases (�bd=0.0005), G-PINNs reduced relative L2 error to about 13% and 14% for stationary and moving shocks, versus 45% and 33% for standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on 1D Burgers test cases, so robustness on higher-dimensional or more complex turbulent flows still needs validation.
paper_title: G-PINNs: Gaussian-based spatially weighted formulation for PINNs: 1D low-viscous Burgers
